author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract A systematic study of nonadaptive hypergeometric group testing designs for identifying two defectives is presented Bounds are given for the number of items that can be tested in a given number of tests Constructions of some classes of designs are presented

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Valuation is a fundamental task of government forprofit and notforprofit business A major subset of valuation issues concerns situations where decision alternatives may be described by benefits and costs and the objective is to infer the values respondent attach to benefitcost levels For studies of this sort computer administration enables the course of data collection to depend on prior responses which allows the study to adapt to responses made by subjects This capability is very useful when the objective is to identify which coefficients to include in a model eg whether to include interaction terms A disadvantage of computer administration however is that presenting many alternatives in a single presentation may not be possible because limited screen real estate may sharply limit the number of attributes and alternatives that may appear in choice sets This paper shows how attribute and attribute level subsetting may be used to create choice sets for use in choicebased evaluation studies sequentially Initially data are collected and the model fit tested for main effects If main effects model gives a good fit conclusions are drawn on main effects Otherwise more choice sets will be included data are collected and the model fit tested for main effects and twoway interactions If that model fits conclusions are drawn on main effects and twoway interactions Otherwise more data collected with added choice sets and conclusions are drawn on main effects twoway and threeway interactions c Elsevier BV

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: The paper aims to find variance balanced and variance partially balanced incomplete block designs when observations within blocks are autocorrelated and we call them BIBAC and PBIBAC designs Orthogonal arrays of type I and type II when used as BIBAC designs have smaller average variance of elementary contrasts of treatment effects compared to the corresponding Balanced Incomplete Block BIB designs with homoscedastic uncorrelated errors The relative efficiency of BIB designs compared to BIBAC designs depends on the block size k and the autocorrelation p and is independent of the number of treatments Further this relative efficiency increases with increasing k Partially balanced incomplete block designs with autocorrelated errors are introduced using partially balanced incomplete block designs and orthogonal arrays of type I and type II C Elsevier BV All rights

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: The main purpose of this paper is fourfold First to prove that the best upper bound on the number of mutually orthogonal Fn F squares is n m where mn m Second to show that this upper bound is achievable if m m is a prime or prime power and m h Third to present a set of four mutually orthogonal F F squares design This latter design is important because there are no orthogonal Latin squares of order which could be used for this purpose Fourth to indicate a method of composing orthogonal F F squares designs In addition we have pointed out the way one may construct orthogonal fractional factorial designs and orthogonal arrays from these designs

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: PTraditional and choicebased conjoint analyses CAs have used full or fractional factorial designs to generate concept profile descriptions However these designs confound two factors when costs are associated with attributes first is the total cost of the concept profile and second is the allocation of costs among the attributes Both factors may influence consumers preferences So far these issues have not been separated in the CA literature The present paper shows how mixtureamount designs used in industrial experiments may be used to separate amount and mixture effects in traditional CA The extension to choicebased CA using balance incomplete block BIB designs is also given

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: In behavioral experiments the respondents make their choices based on several factors called attributes When the attributes are related to benefits and costs and respondents choose one attribute at a time the highest level for benefit attributes and the lowest level for cost attributes will be selected The relative importance given by the respondents to the attributes is not determined If a set of profiles factorial treatment combinations of the attributes is given to the respondents to choose it is possible to determine the relative importance of the attributes under some conditions If the choice set has a dominating profile or dominated profile almost surely that profile will be selected or not selected Thus the set of profiles given to the respondent known as the choice set should not have dominating or dominated profiles Choice sets with no dominating or dominated profiles axe called Pareto optimal subsets In this paper we consider the connectedness and optimality of designs with Pareto optimal choice sets for n attributes each at levels Balanced incomplete block designs are helpful to reduce the choice set sizes without sacrificing optimality and this paper shows some interesting application of them

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Sufficient conditions are given for balanced incomplete block designs with block sizes three and four to be saturated minimal fractions of m items taken in mixture sizes of n and for estimating the contrasts of item means and twoitem specific mixing effects Such fractions are useful for investigations involving mixtures of crops drugs marketing practices and other systems using mixtures of items The balanced incomplete block design with parameters v and k is shown to be a saturated minimal fraction for estimating contrasts of item means and twoitem and threeitem specific mixing effects This is a continuation of the work of Federer Raghavarao and Federer

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the properties and applications of Balanced and Partially Balanced Incomplete Block Designs BIBDs and PBIBDs in the presence of autocorrelation errors While traditional design theory often assumes independent errors this assumption may not hold in many practical scenarios such as agricultural experiments or longitudinal studies where observations are correlated over time or space We extend the classical framework of BIBDs to incorporate autocorrelated error structures deriving conditions under which these designs remain efficient and robust By employing advanced statistical techniques including generalized least squares and mixedeffects models we analyze the impact of autocorrelation on estimation and hypothesis testing within these incomplete block designs Through a series of simulations and realworld case studies we demonstrate the advantages of using BIBDs and PBIBDs with autocorrelated errors over standard design approaches Our findings provide valuable insights for researchers aiming to optimize experimental designs in complex environments enhancing the reliability of statistical inferences in the presence of correlation This work contributes to the broader field of design theory offering new methodologies for addressing autocorrelation in incomplete block designs and paving the way for future research on adaptive designs in statistics

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate optimal nonadaptive hypergeometric grouptesting designs specifically aimed at identifying two defective items in a finite population Employing a statistical framework grounded in combinatorial optimization we develop several grouptesting methodologies that minimize the expected number of tests required for accurate detection of defectives Our focus on nonadaptive designs allows for the formulation of testing procedures without prior knowledge of the outcomes of previous tests enhancing practical applicability in scenarios where immediate feedback is unavailable We derive explicit formulas for the probability of detection and analyze the tradeoffs between test efficiency and the number of groups formed Additionally we establish criteria for the selection of group sizes and test configurations that yield optimal performance under the hypergeometric distribution assumption Our simulations corroborate theoretical findings showcasing significant improvements over traditional testing approaches This research contributes to the broader field of diagnostic testing and quality control offering robust strategies for efficiently identifying defective items in various applications

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn this paper we extend the theoretical framework of Fsquares design a systematic approach to experimental design that optimizes the estimation of treatment effects while controlling for variability Building on prior research we introduce novel statistical techniques that enhance the efficiency of Fsquares designs in various experimental settings Through comprehensive theoretical derivations and simulation studies we demonstrate the robustness of our proposed methodologies in handling complex interactions and multiple factors Additionally we address the implications of our advancements for realworld applications focusing on fields such as agriculture psychology and medicine Our findings reveal that the new designs not only improve parameter estimation but also reduce the overall number of experimental runs required thus making the design process more costeffective This paper contributes valuable insights to the ongoing discourse in statistical design theory and provides practitioners with a refined toolkit for implementing Fsquares designs in their research

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn marketing and behavioral research conjoint measurement is a widely used technique for estimating consumer preferences across multiple attributes of products or services However traditional conjoint analysis often assumes that attribute levels are independent and unbounded which can lead to unrealistic or impractical preference predictions This paper introduces a novel mixtureamount model that incorporates constraints on attribute levels providing a more flexible framework for capturing the complexities of consumer choice behavior Our approach allows for the modeling of preferences where certain attributes are limited by inherent resource constraints or consumerspecific thresholds enhancing the realism of the analysis We validate our model using simulated data and a realworld case study demonstrating its superior predictive accuracy compared to classical conjoint methods The results indicate that accounting for level constraints significantly influences preference estimation and market simulation outcomes This work contributes to the literature by offering a rigorous statistical framework that aligns more closely with actual consumer decision processes ultimately enabling more effective product design and targeting strategies in practice

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract This paper presents an innovative approach to behavioral experiments by employing Pareto optimal choice sets to enhance decisionmaking analysis in experimental economics We conduct a series of n behavioral experiments where n denotes the size of the choice set and explores the implications of utilizing Pareto optimality as a guiding principle in the design of these sets Our methodology entails generating choice sets that offer a range of alternatives ensuring that no alternative can be made better without making at least one other alternative worsethereby establishing a framework that accentuates participant preferences effectively Through rigorous statistical analysis we investigate how participants navigate choices within these Pareto optimal sets examining key metrics such as choice consistency utility maximization and preference stability across varying contexts The findings reveal significant insights into the interplay between optimality and behavioral tendencies demonstrating that participants exhibit greater decision satisfaction reduced cognitive load and enhanced outcome predictability when presented with Pareto optimal options This study contributes to the broader understanding of choice architecture and offers practical implications for the design of decisionmaking environments in fields ranging from economics to behavioral science

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract In the realm of experimental design Balanced Incomplete Block Designs BIBDs serve as a pivotal framework for efficiently allocating treatments across experimental units This paper investigates the conditions under which BIBDs qualify as Minimal Fractional Combinatorial Treatment Designs MFCTDs We establish a set of sufficient conditions that ensure BIBDs retain their design balance while being optimized for fractional replication of treatments By leveraging statistical properties such as the incidence matrix and the dual relationship between treatments and blocks the paper derives theoretical foundations and practical implications that bridge traditional BIBDs and the emerging concepts of fractional combinatorial designs Through illustrative examples and combinatorial proofs we demonstrate the robustness of our findings across varying parameters Our results not only enhance the understanding of the structural intricacies of BIBDs but also offer a pathway for their application in diverse fields including agriculture clinical trials and industrial experimentation where resource constraints necessitate careful treatment allocation This study thus contributes to the ongoing discourse on experimental design providing insights that could lead to more efficient and balanced assessments in factorial experiments

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractThis paper explores design strategies for sequential choice experiments SCEs that assess preferences for economic alternatives Given the complexity involved in decisionmaking processes particularly in scenarios where alternatives evolve over time we propose a framework that integrates empirical insights from behavioral economics and advanced statistical methodologies The study begins by reviewing traditional choice experiment designs and the limitations they present when capturing dynamic preferences We introduce a novel sequential design approach that allows for the identification of both static and dynamic elements of consumer preferences emphasizing the relevance of context and timing in decision outcomes Through Monte Carlo simulations we test various designs to evaluate their efficiency in estimating key preference parameters Results indicate that our proposed designs markedly improve the precision of estimates while reducing respondent burden We illustrate the application of these strategies using a case study involving renewable energy options demonstrating their practical utility in capturing nuanced consumer preferences Our findings contribute to the methodological advancements in choice modeling providing researchers and practitioners with robust tools for understanding decisionmaking in economic contexts

text: Though the analysis of two three and fourway nonorthogonal layouts is available in literature it involves tedious calculations and experimenters refrain using higherway nonorthogonal layouts where computer facilities are not available This paper will show that the analysis of a nway layout can be considered as the analysis of a n layout with covariance and this approach is expected to minimize the calculations when the analysis has to be carried through desk calculators

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: In this paper we give a class of rowcolumn designs with the property that the ith row and the jth column have precisely r treatments in common A conjecture that such designs are quasifactorial is disproved by showing that the designs given in this paper are not quasifactorial It is also shown that the designs given here are nearly optimal

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive study of Overall Aoptimal Balanced Incomplete Block Designs BIBDs which are crucial in the field of experimental design for optimizing the estimation of treatment effects We explore the theoretical underpinnings of Aoptimality focusing on the conditions and parameters that enhance the efficiency of these designs Our findings demonstrate that Overall Aoptimal BIBDs minimize the average variance of the estimated treatment effects across the entire parameter space thereby leading to improved statistical inference in experimental settings Using a combination of combinatorial design theory and optimization techniques we derive explicit constructions of these designs and provide algorithms for their implementation A series of simulation studies validate our theoretical results illustrating the practical advantages of employing Overall Aoptimal designs in comparison to traditional methods We also discuss the implications of our findings for various application domains including agriculture and clinical trials The paper concludes with future research directions and opens avenues for further exploration of optimal designs in complex experimental frameworks Keywords Aoptimality Balanced Incomplete Block Designs Experimental Design Statistical Inference Combinatorial Design

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract In the realm of experimental design Balanced Incomplete Block Designs BIBDs provide a systematic approach for handling situations where not all treatments can be tested in every block This paper investigates the nuanced characteristics that allow for the differentiation among various BIBDs that incorporate repeated blocks We establish a comprehensive framework for categorizing these designs based on parameters such as block size treatment replication and the overall structure of block configurations By leveraging combinatorial design theory and statistical analysis techniques we derive key properties that inform the optimal selection of a BIBD under conditions of incomplete replication Furthermore we present simulation studies to illustrate the practical implications of our findings and elucidate how the proposed distinguishing characteristics can guide researchers in experimental planning Our results emphasize the importance of understanding both the theoretical underpinnings and the practical applications of BIBDs with repeated blocks paving the way for more robust experimental designs in various fields of study

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn the context of experimental design the presence of heterogeneity can significantly impact the validity of statistical inferences This paper introduces a novel class of Designs of Experiments DoE aimed at achieving twoway elimination of heterogeneity We propose a systematic framework that incorporates both randomization and stratification principles to address the dual challenges of variability in treatment effects and subject characteristics The methodology is illustrated through a comprehensive simulation study that demonstrates its effectiveness in reducing bias and increasing the precision of estimators in the presence of heterogeneous populations We also present theoretical insights into the statistical properties of the proposed designs including their robustness and efficiency in various experimental settings Through empirical validation the findings highlight the advantages of adopting this class of Do designs over traditional approaches particularly in fields such as agriculture medicine and social sciences where heterogeneous responses are prevalent This paper contributes to the ongoing discourse on enhancing the reliability of experimental results and provides practitioners with practical guidelines for implementing the proposed designs in realworld scenarios

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn experimental design the analysis of nonorthogonal layouts poses significant challenges due to the complexities introduced by the interdependence of factors Traditional methods often yield biased estimates and reduced statistical power necessitating alternative approaches This paper explores the application of Analysis of Covariance ANCOVA as a robust alternative for handling nonorthogonal designs We meticulously examine the framework of ANCOVA detailing its capacity to adjust for covariates and account for variability thereby enhancing the accuracy of parameter estimates in the presence of nonorthogonality Through a series of simulation studies and realworld examples we demonstrate the effectiveness of ANCOVA in estimating treatment effects while controlling for confounding variables Our findings indicate that ANCOVA not only improves the precision of statistical inferences but also broadens the applicability of results in various scientific fields This study advocates for the integration of ANCOVA in the analysis of nonorthogonal layouts providing a comprehensive framework that facilitates more reliable interpretations of experimental data Keywords Analysis of Covariance ANCOVA nonorthogonal layouts experimental design statistical inference

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract The class of balanced incomplete block designs with parameters b r k considered here includes designs with repeated blocks Attention to date has centered on constructing the members of and on finding the minimum number of distinct blocks d b Under the classical model the usual statistical characteristics do not distinguish among members of however effects related to block totals can be used as distinguishing characteristics A competing effects model is introduced and is shown to distinguish among members of This model is appropriate for intercropping marketing and survey investigations The model is applied to the ten nonisomorphic BIB designs with parameters A computer algorithm for obtaining the pairwise treatment by block incidence matrix of this model is given

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract A necessary and sufficient condition is given to determine overall Aoptimality between a balanced incomplete block design and its complementary design The overall Aoptimal balanced incomplete block design for a given number of treatments is determined These characterizations are provided through simple arithmetical conditions on the parameters of the design

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce and explore the concept of Nested Youden Square Designs a sophisticated statistical framework designed to enhance the efficiency and flexibility of experimental design in agricultural and industrial applications Building on the traditional Youden square design we propose a nested structure that accommodates multiple factors while allowing for an intuitive representation of treatments at various levels of hierarchy Our methodology incorporates the principles of randomization and replication thereby improving the accuracy of treatment comparisons and enabling better control of variability within experimental conditions We provide a comprehensive analysis of the statistical properties of Nested Youden Square Designs including variance estimation treatment effects and power analysis Using simulations and realworld case studies we demonstrate the advantages of our proposed design in terms of robustness and the ability to draw meaningful inferences from complex data sets This study contributes to the field of experimental design by offering a novel approach that is both practical for practitioners and theoretically sound for statisticians paving the way for future research and application in various domains

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive exploration of experimental designs tailored to investigate availability effects and cross effects within the context of a single attribute Availability effects referring to the influence of easily recalled or accessible information on judgment and decisionmaking pose significant challenges in empirical research particularly when quantifying their interplay with cross effectswhere the evaluation of one attribute impacts the perception of another Our study proposes a series of innovative experimental designs that leverage factorial frameworks randomization techniques and advanced statistical modeling to isolate and measure these effects effectively We demonstrate the applicability of our designs through a series of simulations and realworld experiments showcasing their robustness in various scenarios The findings underscore the necessity of appropriately structured experimental setups to unravel the complexities of consumer behavior and decisionmaking processes related to availability and cross effects This paper contributes to the literature by providing both theoretical insights and practical guidance for researchers seeking to advance their understanding of attributebased effects in decision theory

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: When some treatments checks are replicated r times and other treatments new treatments are replicated less than r times an augmented design may be used These designs may be minimum variance designs for estimating contrasts of check effects of new variety effects of new variety versus checks or of all check and new varieties simultaneously In this paper optimal augmented block and optimal augmented rowcolumn designs for estimating certain contrasts of new treatments are presented

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: We show that the balanced crossover designs given by Patterson Biometrika are a universally optimal UO for the joint estimation of direct and residual effects when the competing class is the class of connected binary designs and b UO for the estimation of direct residual effects when the competing class of designs is the class of connected designs which includes the connected binary designs in which no treatment is given to the same subject in consecutive periods In both results the formulation of UO is as given by Shah and Sinha Unpublished manuscript Further we introduce a functional of practical interest involving both direct and residual effects and establish c optimality of Pattersons designs with respect to this functional when the class of competing designs is as in b above

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: In this paper models for brand effects and cross effects based on their availability at specified levels of a single attribute were introduced and designs which enable the estimation of the parameters in that model were presented

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: In this article we characterize Doptimal designs for sn symmetric factorial experiments when observations within blocks are correlated The motivation to this problem lies in a pharmaceutical experiment where the experimenter needed to develop a oncedaily tablet using a factorial design These experiments are usually conducted in healthy human volunteers and the bioavailability is estimated Since each subject is administered more than one formulation the observations within subjects are correlated We provide an explicit construction of Doptimal designs for sn factorial experiment with blocks of size s or multiples of s where observations within blocks are correlated We discuss in detail the construction of optimal designs for n factorial experiments We also provide an analytical proof of the Doptimality when there exist a pair of blocks of odd size and remaining blocks are of even size C Elsevier BV

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Identifying differentially expressed genes is a basic objective in microarray experiments Many statistical methods for detecting differentially expressed genes in multipleslide experiments have been proposed However sometimes with limited experimental resources only a single cDNA array or two Oligonuleotide arrays could be made or only insufficient replicated arrays could be conducted Many current statistical models cannot be used because of the nonavailability of replicated data Simply using fold changes is also unreliable and inefficient Chen et al Ratiobased decisions and the quantitative analysis of cDNA microarray images J Biomed Optics Newton et al On differential variability of expression ratios improving statistical inference about gene expression changes from microarray data J Comput Biol Pan et al How many replicates of arrays are required to detect gene expression changes in microarray experiments a mixture model approach Genome Biol research We propose a new method If the logtransformed ratios for the expressed genes as well as unexpressed genes have equal variance we use a Hadamard matrix to construct a ttest from a single array data Basically we test whether each doubtful gene has significantly differential expression compared to the unexpressed genes We form some new random variables corresponding to the rows of a Hadamard matrix using the algebraic sum of gene expressions A onesample ttest is constructed and the pvalue is calculated for each doubtful gene based on these random variables By using any method for multiple testing adjusted pvalues could be obtained from original pvalues and significance of doubtful genes can be determined When the variance of expressed genes differs from the variance of unexpressed genes we construct a zstatistic based on the result from application of Hadamard matrix and find the confidence interval to retain the null hypothesis Using the interval we determine differentially expressed genes This method is also useful for multiple microarrays especially when sufficient replicated data are not available for a traditional ttest We apply our methodology to ApoAI data The results appear to be promising They not only confirm the early known differentially expressed genes but also indicate more genes to be differentially expressed c Elsevier BV

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractThis paper introduces a novel class of augmented rowcolumn designs which extend traditional block design frameworks to enhance experimental efficiency and flexibility We propose a systematic approach to constructing these designs focusing on their application in scenarios where both row and column factors exhibit multiple levels of variability Our methodology incorporates randomization techniques and the incorporation of auxiliary factors thereby allowing for the control of extraneous variation and the improvement of treatment estimation accuracy Through a series of simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate significant improvements in efficiency and interpretability over standard rowcolumn designs The statistical properties of the proposed designs are rigorously analyzed including their robustness to nonhomogeneity and missing data patterns We conclude with practical guidelines for researchers on the implementation of these augmented designs emphasizing their utility in diverse fields such as agricultural experiments clinical trials and industrial processes

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn the realm of genomics the accurate identification of differentially expressed genes DEGs from microarray experiments remains a critical challenge due to the intricate nature of highdimensional data and the presence of noise This paper introduces innovative Hadamard matrix methods as a novel statistical framework for enhancing the detection of DEGs We first demonstrate how Hadamard transforms can be utilized to optimize the representation of microarray data facilitating efficient data compression while preserving essential biological signals Subsequently we employ a series of statistical tests informed by Hadamard matrix properties resulting in improved power to detect DEGs compared to traditional methods The proposed approach is rigorously validated through extensive simulations and applied to realworld microarray datasets showcasing its robustness and accuracy Our findings indicate that Hadamard matrix methods significantly reduce false discovery rates thereby yielding a higher proportion of true positive identifications This work not only contributes a valuable toolset for genomic data analysis but also highlights the potential of combinatorial matrix techniques in addressing complex biological questions

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn the field of experimental design the influence of correlation among observations within blocks poses significant challenges to the efficiency of factorial experiments This paper investigates the construction of optimal Sn factorial designs when the observations within blocks exhibit correlation thus deviating from the assumption of independence that underpins traditional design methodologies We propose a systematic approach to derive these designs by utilizing advanced statistical techniques including both theoretical frameworks and computational algorithms Our findings demonstrate how to optimize the partitioning of factors in relation to the structure of correlation thereby enhancing the precision of estimated effects and facilitating more reliable inference Simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed designs in various scenarios revealing notable improvements in estimation efficiency and reduction in bias compared to conventional designs The implications of this work extend to a variety of fields where factorial experiments are employed providing a robust tool for researchers facing the complexities of correlated data

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn contemporary statistical practice the design of experiments is crucial for deriving valid inferences from data This paper introduces the concept of Augmented Designs a novel framework that extends traditional experimental designs by incorporating additional layers of flexibility and precision We explore the integration of auxiliary information and adaptive strategies to enhance the robustness of experimental outcomes Our approach leverages techniques from both classical design theory and modern computational methods allowing for the optimization of treatment allocation and the effective management of resources Through a series of simulations and realworld case studies we demonstrate that Augmented Designs significantly improve statistical power and efficiency in inference particularly in scenarios involving complex data structures or heterogeneous response patterns The findings indicate that this framework not only aids in achieving more reliable results but also provides practitioners with intuitive tools for planning and executing experiments Our discussion highlights potential implications for various fields including agriculture medicine and social sciences suggesting that Augmented Designs could pave the way for more effective experimental methodologies in future research

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract This paper explores the universal optimality of Pattersons crossover designs within the framework of statistical experimental design Crossover designs characterized by their ability to allow each experimental unit to serve as its own control offer significant advantages in efficiency and precision when studying treatment effects over time We establish a comprehensive theoretical foundation for Pattersons designs demonstrating their optimality properties across a range of criteria including balancedness efficiency and robustness against variations in treatment effects Utilizing both theoretical derivations and simulation studies we compare Pattersons designs with other commonly used crossover design methodologies Our findings reveal that Pattersons designs consistently maintain optimal performance in minimizing variance and maximizing the power of hypothesis tests thereby justifying their broader adoption in clinical and agricultural research settings Additionally we provide insights into practical implementation including software tools and guidelines for researchers seeking to leverage these designs in their own studies This paper contributes to the ongoing discourse on experimental design by reaffirming the relevance of Pattersons crossover designs and offering a rigorous assessment of their universal optimality in addressing complex experimental challenges

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract In this paper we introduce a novel class of combinatorial designs tailored for applications in group testing a method widely utilized in medical screening and quality control processes Our research develops new constructions of combinatorial designs that optimize the efficiency of detecting defective items within a larger population while minimizing the number of tests required We leverage the properties of these designs to enhance the robustness of group testing scenarios particularly in the context of varying group sizes and known defect rates Through comprehensive analytical methods we establish the combinatorial properties and statistical efficiencies of the proposed designs showcasing their superiority over traditional testing protocols in simulated environments We further explore the implications of our findings for practical applications including largescale disease screening and fault detection in manufacturing Our results demonstrate that the integration of these innovative combinatorial designs into group testing frameworks significantly reduces testing costs and improves detection accuracy paving the way for future advancements in both theoretical and applied statistics

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract A class of designs with property Ct are introduced for the first time and their applications in group testing of samples are studied

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: A number of specific augmented nrow by ncolumn designs for n for v replicated check varieties and for v unreplicated new varieties are presented Three generalizations of the designs for any n are presented with the statistical analysis procedures being given in detail for two of them Formulae for the average variance of a difference between two unreplicated varieties is presented for three classes of designs The effect of increasing n on the average variance is exhibited for two of the classes Many of the designs are constructed to have the unreplicated plots surrounded by either or replicated check varieties and to have roughly onehalf or more of the plots allocated to unreplicated varieties One member of this group of designs has been utilized in field experiments in Brazil

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: We introduce a class of crossover designs with residual effects for experimental situations in which primary interest centres on the comparison of several test treatments to a control treatment rather than on all pairwise comparisons among the treatments We shall call these designs control balanced residual effects designs Their structure is studied in detail some methods of their construction are given and their relative efficiencies are evaluated

text: AbstractThis paper explores design strategies for sequential choice experiments SCEs that assess preferences for economic alternatives Given the complexity involved in decisionmaking processes particularly in scenarios where alternatives evolve over time we propose a framework that integrates empirical insights from behavioral economics and advanced statistical methodologies The study begins by reviewing traditional choice experiment designs and the limitations they present when capturing dynamic preferences We introduce a novel sequential design approach that allows for the identification of both static and dynamic elements of consumer preferences emphasizing the relevance of context and timing in decision outcomes Through Monte Carlo simulations we test various designs to evaluate their efficiency in estimating key preference parameters Results indicate that our proposed designs markedly improve the precision of estimates while reducing respondent burden We illustrate the application of these strategies using a case study involving renewable energy options demonstrating their practical utility in capturing nuanced consumer preferences Our findings contribute to the methodological advancements in choice modeling providing researchers and practitioners with robust tools for understanding decisionmaking in economic contexts

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn experimental design the analysis of nonorthogonal layouts poses significant challenges due to the complexities introduced by the interdependence of factors Traditional methods often yield biased estimates and reduced statistical power necessitating alternative approaches This paper explores the application of Analysis of Covariance ANCOVA as a robust alternative for handling nonorthogonal designs We meticulously examine the framework of ANCOVA detailing its capacity to adjust for covariates and account for variability thereby enhancing the accuracy of parameter estimates in the presence of nonorthogonality Through a series of simulation studies and realworld examples we demonstrate the effectiveness of ANCOVA in estimating treatment effects while controlling for confounding variables Our findings indicate that ANCOVA not only improves the precision of statistical inferences but also broadens the applicability of results in various scientific fields This study advocates for the integration of ANCOVA in the analysis of nonorthogonal layouts providing a comprehensive framework that facilitates more reliable interpretations of experimental data Keywords Analysis of Covariance ANCOVA nonorthogonal layouts experimental design statistical inference

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractCrossover designs are a robust statistical methodology utilized in clinical trials and experimental research for comparing the effects of treatments against a control condition This paper explores the efficacy of various crossover design strategies in the context of treatment control comparisons emphasizing their advantages in reducing variability and improving the precision of treatment effect estimates We systematically review existing models and methodologies highlighting the assumptions and analytical techniques underlying crossover designs Using simulation studies we demonstrate the impact of design factors such as carryover effects washout periods and sequence randomization on the treatment comparison outcomes We also propose a new framework for assessing the power and sample size requirements specific to crossover trials alongside guidance for researchers in selecting appropriate designs based on study objectives and practical constraints Our findings illustrate that when thoughtfully implemented crossover designs significantly enhance the sensitivity of trials facilitating more efficient identification of effective treatments while controlling for intersubject variability This paper serves as a comprehensive guide for researchers interested in applying crossover designs to treatment comparisons ultimately contributing to more rigorous and reliable scientific inquiry in clinical and experimental settings

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract This paper investigates the phenomenon of untruthful answering within the context of repeated randomizedresponse procedures a methodology designed to elicit truthful responses to sensitive questions while preserving respondent privacy We analyze the impact of factors such as respondent demographics perceived anonymity and question sensitivity on the likelihood of providing dishonest answers across multiple iterations of randomizedresponse techniques Utilizing a combination of theoretical modeling and empirical data from a series of surveys we identify key patterns of behavior and establish statistical benchmarks for assessing the reliability of responses Our findings highlight significant variability in response accuracy suggesting that repeated applications of randomizedresponse methods do not uniformly induce truthful reporting We also propose modifications to the design and implementation of these procedures to enhance their effectiveness in collecting honest data This research contributes to the broader literature on survey methodology by providing insights into the limitations of current practices and offering recommendations for future studies aiming to mitigate untruthful responses

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract In this paper we explore the universal optimality of uniform experimental UE designs within the context of competing effects models Competing effects models are widely applicable in various fields including biomedical research and social sciences where multiple factors may influence a response variable simultaneously We demonstrate that UE designs serve as a robust tool for maximizing the efficiency of parameter estimation under these complex modeling scenarios Through theoretical derivations and empirical simulations we establish that these designs not only yield lower mean squared errors compared to traditional design approaches but also exhibit superior robustness against potential model misspecifications We further investigate the properties of UE designs in different statistical environments including highdimensional settings and varying sample sizes Our findings highlight the versatility and efficiency of UE designs reinforcing their status as universally optimal in managing competing effects while ensuring precise inferences This study contributes to the field of experimental design by providing a comprehensive framework for applying UE designs in challenging statistical scenarios ultimately enhancing the reliability of conclusions drawn from complex data structures

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract A systematic study of nonadaptive hypergeometric group testing designs for identifying two defectives is presented Bounds are given for the number of items that can be tested in a given number of tests Constructions of some classes of designs are presented

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: A simple and clear procedure is given that allows to some degree the estimation and testing of the probability of an untruthful answer in addition to estimating the population proportion by using Warners randomized response technique twice

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate optimal nonadaptive hypergeometric grouptesting designs specifically aimed at identifying two defective items in a finite population Employing a statistical framework grounded in combinatorial optimization we develop several grouptesting methodologies that minimize the expected number of tests required for accurate detection of defectives Our focus on nonadaptive designs allows for the formulation of testing procedures without prior knowledge of the outcomes of previous tests enhancing practical applicability in scenarios where immediate feedback is unavailable We derive explicit formulas for the probability of detection and analyze the tradeoffs between test efficiency and the number of groups formed Additionally we establish criteria for the selection of group sizes and test configurations that yield optimal performance under the hypergeometric distribution assumption Our simulations corroborate theoretical findings showcasing significant improvements over traditional testing approaches This research contributes to the broader field of diagnostic testing and quality control offering robust strategies for efficiently identifying defective items in various applications

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive study of Overall Aoptimal Balanced Incomplete Block Designs BIBDs which are crucial in the field of experimental design for optimizing the estimation of treatment effects We explore the theoretical underpinnings of Aoptimality focusing on the conditions and parameters that enhance the efficiency of these designs Our findings demonstrate that Overall Aoptimal BIBDs minimize the average variance of the estimated treatment effects across the entire parameter space thereby leading to improved statistical inference in experimental settings Using a combination of combinatorial design theory and optimization techniques we derive explicit constructions of these designs and provide algorithms for their implementation A series of simulation studies validate our theoretical results illustrating the practical advantages of employing Overall Aoptimal designs in comparison to traditional methods We also discuss the implications of our findings for various application domains including agriculture and clinical trials The paper concludes with future research directions and opens avenues for further exploration of optimal designs in complex experimental frameworks Keywords Aoptimality Balanced Incomplete Block Designs Experimental Design Statistical Inference Combinatorial Design

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn the realm of statistical analysis the management of heterogeneity within experimental designs is critical for ensuring valid and reliable results This paper explores a novel framework for analyzing connectedness in twoway elimination of heterogeneity designs contributing to the optimization of experimental efficiency and robustness We propose a systematic approach that integrates the principles of connectedness with twoway designs allowing for a deeper understanding of the underlying structures in heterogeneous data Utilizing advanced statistical techniques we demonstrate how this framework can be applied to various fields including behavioral sciences medical research and social sciences where heterogeneity is prevalent Through a series of simulations and realworld case studies we illustrate the advantages of our method in mitigating the effects of unobserved heterogeneity while enhancing the interpretability of interaction effects Our findings reveal that connectedness plays a pivotal role in the performance of twoway designs leading to more accurate estimations of treatment effects and facilitating robust inferential processes This study not only lays the groundwork for future research on connectedness in statistical designs but also provides practical guidelines for practitioners seeking to improve the design and analysis of heterogeneous data

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn the context of experimental design the presence of heterogeneity can significantly impact the validity of statistical inferences This paper introduces a novel class of Designs of Experiments DoE aimed at achieving twoway elimination of heterogeneity We propose a systematic framework that incorporates both randomization and stratification principles to address the dual challenges of variability in treatment effects and subject characteristics The methodology is illustrated through a comprehensive simulation study that demonstrates its effectiveness in reducing bias and increasing the precision of estimators in the presence of heterogeneous populations We also present theoretical insights into the statistical properties of the proposed designs including their robustness and efficiency in various experimental settings Through empirical validation the findings highlight the advantages of adopting this class of Do designs over traditional approaches particularly in fields such as agriculture medicine and social sciences where heterogeneous responses are prevalent This paper contributes to the ongoing discourse on enhancing the reliability of experimental results and provides practitioners with practical guidelines for implementing the proposed designs in realworld scenarios

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract In the realm of experimental design Balanced Incomplete Block Designs BIBDs serve as a pivotal framework for efficiently allocating treatments across experimental units This paper investigates the conditions under which BIBDs qualify as Minimal Fractional Combinatorial Treatment Designs MFCTDs We establish a set of sufficient conditions that ensure BIBDs retain their design balance while being optimized for fractional replication of treatments By leveraging statistical properties such as the incidence matrix and the dual relationship between treatments and blocks the paper derives theoretical foundations and practical implications that bridge traditional BIBDs and the emerging concepts of fractional combinatorial designs Through illustrative examples and combinatorial proofs we demonstrate the robustness of our findings across varying parameters Our results not only enhance the understanding of the structural intricacies of BIBDs but also offer a pathway for their application in diverse fields including agriculture clinical trials and industrial experimentation where resource constraints necessitate careful treatment allocation This study thus contributes to the ongoing discourse on experimental design providing insights that could lead to more efficient and balanced assessments in factorial experiments

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Abstract A necessary and sufficient condition is given to determine overall Aoptimality between a balanced incomplete block design and its complementary design The overall Aoptimal balanced incomplete block design for a given number of treatments is determined These characterizations are provided through simple arithmetical conditions on the parameters of the design

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: A subset T of S is said to be a Pareto Optimal subset of m ordered attributes factors if for profiles combination of attribute levels x xm and y ym is an element of T no profile dominates another that is there exists no pair such that xi less than or equal to yi for i m Pareto Optimal designs have specific applications in economics cognitive psychology and marketing research where investigators use main effects linear models to infer how respondents value levels of costs and benefits from their preferences for sets of profiles offered them In such studies it is desirable that no profile dominates the others in a set This paper shows how to construct a Pareto Optimal subset proves that a single Pareto Optimal subset is not a connected main effects plan provides subsets of two or more attributes that are connected in symmetric designs and gives corresponding results for asymmetric designs

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: A necessary and sufficient condition is established for doublyconnectedness in b b row and k k column designs in which all cells are filled A necessary condition for doublyconnectedness in a generalized twoway elimination of heterogeneity designs is provided and a property of doublyconnected designs is given

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: In this paper we give a class of rowcolumn designs with the property that the ith row and the jth column have precisely r treatments in common A conjecture that such designs are quasifactorial is disproved by showing that the designs given in this paper are not quasifactorial It is also shown that the designs given here are nearly optimal

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: AbstractIn many fields of research understanding the main effects of variables on an outcome is crucial for informed decisionmaking This paper introduces a novel framework for estimating main effects through the lens of Pareto optimal subsets We leverage the concept of Pareto efficiency to identify subsets of variables that yield the best tradeoffs between multiple conflicting criteria thereby enhancing the robustness of main effect estimations Our methodology involves a multiobjective optimization approach where we consider both the precision of effect estimates and the complexity of the model We demonstrate the practicality of our framework through extensive simulations and two realworld case studies illustrating its efficiency in handling highdimensional data with potential multicollinearity issues Results indicate that our Pareto optimal subsets not only improve the accuracy of main effect estimates but also facilitate better interpretability of the underlying relationships This work contributes to the fields of statistics and applied data analysis by providing a systematic method for estimating main effects while honoring the tradeoffs inherent in model selection

author: Damaraju Raghavarao
text: Sufficient conditions are given for balanced incomplete block designs with block sizes three and four to be saturated minimal fractions of m items taken in mixture sizes of n and for estimating the contrasts of item means and twoitem specific mixing effects Such fractions are useful for investigations involving mixtures of crops drugs marketing practices and other systems using mixtures of items The balanced incomplete block design with parameters v and k is shown to be a saturated minimal fraction for estimating contrasts of item means and twoitem and threeitem specific mixing effects This is a continuation of the work of Federer Raghavarao and Federer
